decisions.what: harness.js refuses to compile a block name that is not in wp.blocks, instead of letting serialize() drop it.
decisions.why: wp.blocks.createBlock() accepts an unregistered name and wp.blocks.serialize() then emits nothing for that subtree: measured, __compile([{name:'agent/does-not-exist'}]) returned {markup:'',all_valid:true,invalid:[]}. Silent content loss reported as success is the worst possible failure for a compiler. It now returns {error:'block "X" is not registered in this harness; it would serialize to nothing'} at any depth, which is still the pinned CONTRACT.md 6 error envelope. The agent's __registry() diff remains the primary gap detector; this is the backstop for when it is not consulted.

decisions.what: Agent block packages must declare supports.autoRegister:true; the shipped fixture does.
decisions.why: A dynamic block ships no editor script, so nothing calls registerBlockType() for it client-side and the harness cannot compile trees that use it. WordPress 7.0 added the opt-in: _wp_enqueue_auto_register_blocks() lists such blocks in window.__unstableAutoRegisterBlocks and registerCoreBlocks() registers them from the server-side bootstrap with a ServerSideRender edit. That hook hangs off enqueue_block_editor_assets, which the harness fires, so it works with no harness-side special casing. Proven: after installing agent-testimonial.zip, agent/testimonial appears in __registry() and compiles to '<!-- wp:agent/testimonial {"quote":"Compiled by the harness"} /-->'. Without the flag the block is a registry gap.

decisions.what: The tokens response carries two keys beyond the contract three: adapter_notes (string[]) and theme_file_written (bool), plus the compiled settings.
decisions.why: The contract pins {theme_json_written, adapters_applied, fingerprint}; the agent side parses that with a non-strict zod object, so extra keys are dropped rather than rejected. adapter_notes is the only way a caller can see WHY an adapter no-opped, which is the difference between 'Kadence took the palette' and 'Kadence silently ignored you'.

specs/companion-plugin.spec.json M6 acceptance says adapters_applied includes 'kadence'. x-agent's mock companion answers 'kadence-blocks', but that is a fixture in their own test, not a wire contract -- the real client passes adapters_applied through untouched.

decisions.what: POST /snapshot/export lives in class-theme-tokens.php next to POST /theme/tokens.
decisions.why: Milestone M6 is 'tokens and export' and the owned-file list has no class-snapshot.php. They are two halves of the same promotion story: one writes the design system in, the other packages the instance out.

decisions.what: Every filesystem mutation goes through WP_Filesystem, with one documented rename() fallback.
decisions.why: Plugin Check flags rename()/rmdir()/is_writable() as errors. WP_Filesystem is also the right answer for hosts whose FS_METHOD is not direct. The single remaining rename() is a last resort inside X_Companion_Block_Library::move(), reached only when WP_Filesystem::move() has already refused, and it carries a phpcs:ignore with the measurement that justifies it. wp plugin check: 0 errors.

decisions.what: tests/test-install.php and tests/test-tokens.php are live-only, and each carries its own ~120-line REST client.
decisions.why: Install, rollback, delete and global-styles writes are filesystem-and-registry behaviour; the only honest oracle is a real instance, and the only honest interface is the wire the agent uses. The client is duplicated and function_exists()-guarded rather than extracted, because a shared include would be a file neither test owns.

decisions.what: harness.spec.ts runs on node's built-in test runner and node's native TypeScript stripping.
decisions.why: No @playwright/test, no tsx, no build step: the only dependency is playwright itself, which proof/lib/env.mjs already resolves out of tools/node_modules so one browser download serves the whole repo. tests/package.json declares it pinned at 1.60.0 for anyone running the directory standalone.

decisions.what: run-all.sh honours X_RUNTIME_CORE_ONLY / X_RUNTIME_CORE_PLUS_SUITE to run against instances it did not boot.
decisions.why: tools/.runtime/<profile>-<posture> is shared bookkeeping. With several agents on one machine, another process stopping 'its' core-only-toolchain deletes the descriptor for a live instance and wipes the shared site directory underneath it -- observed twice during this run. The escape hatch lets a caller point the suite at a descriptor it owns; nothing is booted and nothing is stopped in that mode.

deviations.what: The harness request defines WP_ADMIN for itself before init fires, so that is_admin() is true while blocks register. On by default in toolchain posture, off in production; force either way with X_COMPANION_HARNESS_ADMIN_CONTEXT, or the x_companion_harness_admin_context filter. Header X-Harness-Admin-Context reports which happened.
deviations.why: Contract 6.3 says 'for every WP_Block_Type, enqueue all handles in editor_script_handles'. Measured against Kadence Blocks 3.7.9.1: those handles are declared by the block types but only REGISTERED from an init callback whose first line is 'if ( ! is_admin() ) return;'. A REST request is not admin, so by the time the harness route runs the handles do not exist, wp_script_is() is false, and all 59 kadence/* blocks are missing from wp.blocks -- measured, registry 113 with the suite installed, identical to core-only. That is not the client-side registration failure 6 anticipates and answers with the __registry() diff; it is a server-side gate, and it is fixable server-side. Defining WP_ADMIN is enough (verified: registry 176, 59/59 kadence blocks, kadence/rowlayout trees compile all_valid). Blast radius is small because admin_init is fired by wp-admin/admin.php, which is not in play: only code that asks is_admin() sees a difference, on a route whose entire job is to be the editor minus the editor. Production posture keeps literal 6 behaviour.

deviations.what: NOT DONE. The Kadence tree is exercised by tests/harness.spec.ts, built at runtime from the live manifest, instead of committed as a validator fixture.
deviations.why: tests/test-validator.php globs fixtures/trees/*.json and validates every one against fixtures/registry-snapshot.json, which holds 15 core blocks and no Kadence. A kadence tree there produces E_UNKNOWN_BLOCK, so the 'expected' file would have to encode failure and a fixture named valid-kadence would assert valid:false. Making it genuinely valid needs the Kadence blocks added to registry-snapshot.json -- a file this agent does not own, and one that tests/test-manifest.php:488 pins with x_assert_same( 4, $manifest['counts']['dynamic_blocks'] ). Kadence blocks are all dynamic, so adding them breaks a passing test in someone else's milestone. Left for a coordinated change. The tree that compiles cleanly, for whoever picks it up: [{name:'kadence/rowlayout',attributes:{uniqueID:'xc-row-1',columns:2},innerBlocks:[{name:'kadence/column',attributes:{uniqueID:'xc-col-1'},innerBlocks:[{name:'core/paragraph',attributes:{content:'Left'}}]},{name:'kadence/column',attributes:{uniqueID:'xc-col-2'},innerBlocks:[{name:'core/paragraph',attributes:{content:'Right'}}]}]}]

deviations.spec_ref: M4 acceptance: '__registry() superset-of manifest.blocks keys for core'
deviations.what: Three core blocks are asserted as an exact expected-missing set rather than required to be present: core/legacy-widget, core/post-comments, core/widget-group.
deviations.why: They are registered server-side but registerCoreBlocks() never registers them client-side -- widget-bridge infrastructure and a deprecated alias, none of which an agent should ever emit. The set is pinned exactly (deepEqual, not a subset check), so losing any further block fails the assertion. agent/* is excluded from the same check on purpose: an installed agent block only reaches wp.blocks when it declares supports.autoRegister, which is the registry gap the next case tests.

deviations.what: The filesystem theme.json write is off unless X_COMPANION_TOKENS_WRITE_THEME_FILE is defined true, even when the theme directory is writable.
deviations.why: The contract calls the user-origin global styles CPT the primary path and this makes it the only path by default. Playground's theme directory IS writable, so a 'write the file when you can' rule would rewrite the active theme's theme.json on every token apply -- a destructive side effect nobody asked for, and one that makes the CPT path untested. theme_json_written reports the CPT write; theme_file_written reports the optional one.
